subject: Meridian Health: request for rigid multi-region DR RTO/RPO commitments
messages:
From: Jake Ortiz <jake.ortiz@meridianhealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Meridian Security <sec@meridianhealth.com>, Meridian Procurement <procurement@meridianhealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: URGENT: DR/RTO/RPO commitments needed for contract

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week. Meridian is pushing on firm guarantees around cross-region failover for our production workloads. We need to understand whether Redwood can commit to: 

- Automated multi-region failover with an RTO <= 5 minutes for the primary user-facing API
- RPO of 0 minutes for transaction/stateful services (or a clear design pattern explaining how data consistency is preserved)
- 99.995% uptime across active/standby regions with documented replication and failover exercises

We're preparing procurement and security approvals and that language is a gating item. I've attached Meridian_DR_requirements.xlsx with our minimal ask. Please let me know whether these numbers are possible as-is, and if not, what the recommended carveouts/options and incremental costs are.

Jake Ortiz
Director, Cloud Platforms
Meridian Health

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Jake Ortiz <jake.ortiz@meridianhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-25T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: DR/RTO/RPO commitments needed for contract

Jake — thanks for the clear doc and for surfacing this early. Short answer: we cannot promise a 5-minute universal cross-region RTO for all workloads without architectural changes and cost/ops tradeoffs. That said, we can offer a tiered approach that meets your business needs with explicit carveouts and fees. Proposal (high level):

1) Warm-standby plan (recommended) — Redwood provisions reserved capacity in a secondary region with continuous replication. For user-facing API endpoints we can target RTO = 15–30 minutes under warm-standby operational playbooks; RPO can be near-zero for write-through replicated stores (database replication dependent).

2) Premium active-active option — for critical endpoints we can architect an active-active deployment with cross-region consensus to approach ~5–10 minute recovery windows for session-level continuity. This requires changes on Meridian's side (stateless frontends, globally routed LB, idempotent writes, and database-level sharding/replication) plus a 20–35% price uplift for reserved capacity + networking.

3) Carveouts and SLA language — propose adding a failover activation window (30 min warm-up) and an exceptions clause for catastrophic regional outages and upstream provider network partitions. We can commit to failover runbooks, quarterly DR exercises, and post-incident RCA within 5 business days.

Next steps: can we schedule a 60-minute technical run-through with your SREs and our infra lead (Laura + Rishi) tomorrow? I'll also circulate a redline SLA draft for legal review.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Jake — quick technical summary from infra:

- For strict <5min failover you need active-active or fully synchronous cross-region replication. Synchronous replication across continental regions increases tail latency and failure surface; most customers opt for async replication with near-zero RPO for critical streams and compensating application logic.

- Token KV caches and prefix caches add complexity — we can persist and pre-warm caches during a failover but cold-cache latency will spike.

- Replica promotion time for our standard nearline replication is typically 8–20 minutes depending on backlog size; under warm-standby with reserved capacity we see stable RTOs in the 12–25 minute range in practice.

- We can instrument an automated health-check driven failover that reduces manual ops time, but legal/contract must accept a defined activation window and assume-scope (which services are in/out).

I'll join the run-through and bring replication metrics and a proposed runbook.

- Laura Bennett
Sr. Director, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

From: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
To: Jake Ortiz <jake.ortiz@meridianhealth.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-26T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: DR/RTO/RPO commitments needed for contract

Jake — from legal/procurement perspective we can support a tiered SLA but need to lock down a few items before signing: 

- Exact list of Meridian services/endpoints that will be covered by the premium SLA (SOW or appendix).
- Explicit activation criteria for Redwood-initiated vs. customer-initiated failover.
- Liability cap tied to monthly committed spend; we cannot accept unlimited credit for availability breaches.
- Auditability: Meridian requires quarterly DR exercise reports and access to runbook outcomes for compliance review.

I've attached a redline with suggested language that preserves indemnity limits and adds a clear failover activation window (30 minutes) and an escalation path. If Meridian needs 5-minute RTOs as a hard contractual commitment we need a signed appendix confirming architecture changes and a dedicated ops SLA (and a higher liability cap).

Evelyn Hart
VP, Legal & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Jake — thanks for the prompt responses. Summary and proposed next steps: 

1) Redwood can offer a formal warm-standby SLA (target RTO 15–30m, near-zero RPO for replicated services) as standard with reserved capacity.
2) For Meridian's hard 5-minute requirement we will prepare a separate active-active engineering appendix and cost estimate (this will include changes on Meridian's side).
3) Legal to confirm appendix language and liability cap; operations to run a joint DR tabletop within 10 business days and a full failover test within 45 days.

Can we lock a technical call for 2027-04-28 10:00 PT? I'll circulate calendar invites and the redlined SLA. If that works I'll also share a scoped estimate for the premium active-active option.

Best,
Karthik
